correctness.rationale: Every depth-one proposition-free counting formula is a Boolean outdegree predicate and therefore has a finite/cofinite exact-degree truth set; conversely every such set is definable. The outdegree is \(\operatorname{Bin}(n-1,\lambda/n)\). A maximal Bernoulli–Poisson coupling gives total-variation distance at most \( (\lambda+\lambda^2)/n \), proving all limiting probabilities, the exact spectrum, and the Hausdorff finite-size bound. Eventual Poisson-tail domination and Stirling asymptotics give compact perfect Cantor topology and zero dimension. Fixing early digits and varying a separated tail prefix gives \(2^{J-O(1)}\) points more than \(\varepsilon\) apart. Since \(-\log t_J\sim J\log J\), the leading precision-entropy constant is exactly \(\log 2\). For \(\lambda<\log2\), the zero-degree mass exceeds one half and creates the explicit gap. Finite exact enumerations and numerical total-variation checks were performed with the bundled checker; these checks are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Search of indexed mathematical findings and primary literature identified no exact fixed-sparse rooted counting-modal Poisson probability spectrum with the sharp logarithmic covering entropy and finite-size Hausdorff bound. The classical Poisson law and Cantor achievement-set criteria are explicitly acknowledged; none alone supplies the joint logical/spectral/entropy assertion. Relevant sources were compared by their probability ensembles, logic syntax, and implications, rather than by title. The accessible portion of the most relevant 2026 paper studies uniform graph counts and high-branching trees, not fixed sparse intensities. This is a qualified priority assessment, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The minimal natural counting-modal fragment detects outdegree and asks what limiting truth proportions can be realized in the sparse graph model motivating model-counting logic. The result answers this invariant completely for every positive fixed intensity, establishes that its closure is a zero-dimensional Cantor set rather than a generic interval, and determines the exact leading metric entropy of attainable-probability approximation as accuracy increases. The \(O(1/n)\) finite-size Hausdorff rate connects limiting expressivity to finite-graph experiments. Precision entropy describes how finely the fragment can calibrate classification confidence, rather than an arbitrary fixed-index extraction.
